text:
B: Hiya! Can you hear me okay?
A: Yes, I can hear you. Hello.
B: Hello, I'm Gemma. Is it Kulwinder?
A: Yes, that's right.
B: Lovely. Erm, did you do the puzzle bit? I was useless at the shapes one.
A: I did it. I read the instructions twice because I wasn't sure if we could go back. You can't, by the way.
B: No, I found that out the hard way, yeah. So whereabouts are you?
A: Hayes. West London. Near Heathrow, so if you hear a plane, that's why.
B: Oh, fair enough. I'm in Taunton, so it's tractors here, not planes. Bit quieter.
A: Mm.
B: Erm, what do you do, then? Sorry, is that alright to ask?
A: It's fine. I'm not working at the moment. I was a tailor, alterations, twenty-odd years. Workrooms in Southall, then a dry-cleaner's counter. I stopped about three years ago. Arthritis in my hands, and my back, and the kids. It sort of all came at once, you know.
B: Oh, that's rough. Hands are your whole job, aren't they, with sewing.
A: Yes. They were. I still do bits for family, school uniform hems, my mum's suits. But I can't do a full day on a machine now, my fingers just lock.
B: Have they got you seeing anyone for it? Physio or a hand clinic or anything?
A: I've got a physio sheet. I do it every morning. You sound like a doctor.
B: Ha, nurse. Sorry, it's a habit. I'm on a surgical ward, so I'm always asking people about their joints.
A: Ah. Okay. That's hard work, nursing. Long hours.
B: Yeah, it is. I'm on twelve-and-a-half-hour days, three in a row this week, so I'm proper knackered today, to be honest. I like it, mostly. The staffing's the hard bit, there's never enough of us, but the patients are lovely, and the students. I've got a couple shadowing me at the minute and they're keen, which helps. You've got kids, did you say?
A: Two. My son's nineteen, he's doing an apprenticeship. My daughter's fifteen, she's got her mocks coming up, so the house is very tense.
B: Oh, GCSEs. I remember that stress. Is she doing alright?
A: She's clever. She just wants pasta every night instead of studying.
B: Ha! I'm the same, to be fair. Pasta bake is basically my whole shift week.
A: I cook dinner properly every night. Dal, roti. Pasta is once a week, that's the deal.
B: That's a good deal. My partner would swap with your daughter in a heartbeat, he loves a curry. Friday's always an Indian takeaway for us.
A: Takeaway. Hmm. You should learn dal, it's easy, and cheaper.
B: Go on then, how do you do it?
A: Chana dal or moong? Haan, it doesn't matter, start with moong, it's quicker. You wash it, you—
B: Oh, is that us? It's saying...
